identity.title: Unveiling the Role of the Magnetic Field at the Smallest Scales of Star Formation

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of polarized dust emission from the protostellar source Ser-emb 8 at a linear resolution of 140 AU.

coordinates.value: RA ~277.45 deg, Dec ~1.278 deg (J2000; from Table 1 positions)

evidence.quote: Ser-emb 8 is one of several low-mass, Class 0 protostars in the Serpens Main star-forming region

question.value: Does the magnetic field in the Class 0 protostar Ser-emb 8 show strong-field (hourglass, large-scale-aligned) morphology at ~100 AU scales, and is it consistent with weakly or strongly magnetized AREPO simulations?

evidence.quote: We conclude that the Ser-emb 8 data are most similar to the weakly magnetized simulations, which exhibit random alignment

analysis_steps.goal: Derive polarization maps and field orientation

method.value: P = sqrt(Q^2+U^2), P/I, chi = 0.5 arctan(U/Q), P debiased; B field taken perpendicular to polarization

evidence.quote: The polarized intensity $P = \sqrt{Q^2 + U^2}$, the fractional polarization $P_\textrm{frac} = P / I$, and the polarization position angle $\chi = 0.5\,\arctan{\left(U / Q\right)}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Run AREPO simulations and make synthetic polarization

method.value: Synthetic Q, U, column density in 3000 AU region around each core, optically thin, 12 AU grid, multiple lines of sight

evidence.quote: we calculate synthetic polarization in a $3000$ AU region centered on each core assuming the optically thin limit.

assumptions.value: Isothermal, ideal MHD; scaled with cs = 0.2 km/s, nH = 1000 cm^-3

evidence.quote: We have scaled our simulations to physical units using a sound speed of $c_{\rm s}=0.2~{\rm km}~{\rm s}^{-1}$ and hydrogen density $n_{\rm H} = 1000~{\rm cm}^{-3}$.

validation.value: Downsampling mock column densities has no significant effect on HRO

evidence.quote: downsampling the mock projected column densities has no significant effect on the computed HRO

analysis_steps.goal: Compute HRO for ALMA and simulations

method.value: Angle between B and Stokes I (or density) gradient per pixel, weighted 1/0 by gradient above median; averaged over lines of sight

evidence.quote: weighting the contribution from each element by a 1 or 0 depending on whether the magnitude of the density gradient is above the median value

evidence.quote: we assume the magnetic field has an orientation that is perpendicular to the measured polarization

results_numeric.quantity: Initial mass-to-flux ratio of the four simulations

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA field in Ser-emb 8 has no hourglass morphology and shows perturbed structure at small scales

evidence.quote: The magnetic field revealed by the ALMA data does not have an hourglass morphology

findings_qualitative.value: HRO of ALMA data is flat, like the weakly magnetized simulations; strong-field HRO peaks at phi = 0

evidence.quote: we find that the HRO of the ALMA observations of Ser-emb 8 is flat, indicating a random field similar to the weakly magnetized simulations

claims.hypothesis: Ser-emb 8 formed in a strongly magnetized environment with an hourglass field
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 7 polarization map compared with four AREPO simulations via HRO
claims.result: No hourglass; flat HRO matching weak-field simulations
claims.finding: Ser-emb 8 formed in a super- or trans-Alfvénic environment where turbulence shapes the material

evidence.quote: we conclude that the turbulence in the natal cloud of Ser-emb 8 is super- or trans-Alfvénic

claims.hypothesis: Cloud-scale field strength determines small-scale field and density structure
claims.experiment: Four AREPO simulations with different initial field strengths
claims.result: Only the 120 uG simulation preserves field direction and shows hourglass below 1000 AU
claims.finding: Only very strong fields yield hourglass and aligned structure

evidence.quote: Only in the very strongly magnetized (sub-Alfvénic) simulation

why_this_method.value: HRO quantifies relation between field and density structure, as used by Planck

evidence.quote: Here we use this technique to shed light on the role of the magnetic field at the $\sim$ 100 AU scale of an individual star-forming core

limitations_admitted.value: Trends in P vs I are weak and could be geometrical; simulations lack outflows, disks, non-ideal MHD

evidence.quote: However, the trends in Figure [4](#fig:P_vs_I) are weak, and could be due to geometrical effects.
